crime_highlights: Ryan Crossley then pushed his shopping cart out of the way and lunged at Mr. Powshuk, stabbing Mr. Powshuk's right side torso and buttocks area with the deer knife multiple times in rapid succession
Ryan Crossley put his hand on Mr. Powshuk's back, grabbing at him by his coat or hi-vis vest, and continued to stab at him repeatedly with the deer knife
Ryan Crossley began forcefully kicking him
rationale_highlights: This Court must consider Ryan Crossley's Aboriginal heritage and take it into account in determining a fit sentence that is proportionate to the seriousness of the offence and his moral blameworthiness
I find that there is likely an indirect causal link between the intergenerational impact experienced Ryan Crossley as a result of his Indigenous background and his drug addiction
I have considered Ryan Crossley's Indigenous heritage, but consider this to be a less significant factor given the seriousness of the offence
I have considered the impacts of his Indigenous heritage as part of my finding that his drug addiction is a mitigating factor in this case
note: Crime passage lacks victim death; death described in paras 27-28.

crime_highlights: Ms. Monk could not be roused and was taken to hospital in Fort St. James for treatment
She had wounds on her left eyelid and the back and right side of her head. Pieces of glass were lodged in her scalp.
Ms. Monk was transported to Vancouver General Hospital but died from her injuries on February 8, 2022
An autopsy confirmed that the cause of her death was blunt force trauma to the head
Mr. Beynon admits that he committed the offence of manslaughter of Ms. Monk by repeatedly striking her in the head or on the head with a bottle
rationale_highlights: I have considered the Gladue principles to be applied in this case

Although not in and of themselves a mitigating factor, the impact of intergenerational trauma resulting from Mr. Beynon's Indigenous background is something that the court is able to consider in determining the extent of his moral culpability
he is a descendent of a number of residential school survivors, including his mother
note: Court only says it may consider factor for culpability; no clear reduction stated.

crime_highlights: The driver shifted the car into reverse and revved the engine. He then reversed the car into the police vehicle.
Police opened the trunk and found Mr. Soderberg.
Under Mr. Soderberg they found a carbine style firearm with a loaded magazine
They found four more firearms inside various bags in the trunk
rationale_highlights: The most significant mitigating factors in this case relate to Mr. Soderberg's experience growing up in Canada as an Indigenous youth from a broken family
I find that systemic and background factors relating to Mr. Soderberg's circumstances as an Indigenous person have played a significant role in bringing him before the court
I find that Mr. Soderberg's moral blameworthiness is diminished by these factors

the prospects for his rehabilitation must be given meaningful consideration in light of past failures by people in authority in his life and the continuing crisis of overrepresentation of Indigenous offenders in custody
In my view, the Crown's proposal does not give adequate effect to the Gladue factors in this case.
note: Firearms case without victim; crime highlights are acts of possession and flight.
